summary: Finished item 'look' after its review. I applied the reviewed look.patch in a fresh worktree, fixed both must_fix findings and the should_fix items that were cheap and clearly right, and wrote a new look.patch. It has 46 files and applies to a clean HEAD, both alone and after checks.patch. (1) must_fix 2: the tools/check_head_ui.py hunk is dropped. (2) must_fix 1: KEYS now catches a key in brackets ('Preview (Space)'), 'hit'/'tap' Enter, Ctrl-S, the Mac's chord signs, Backspace, PgUp/PgDn/Page Up and 'or Return'. It no longer flags net names ('F45 / F12 curves', 'the F7 net') or 'Escape' used as a word. Since the walk cannot reach every shown string, a new code sweep, name_sweep.keys_in_code, reads every sentence in workbench/ that names a key. It sets aside docstrings, comments, keys handed to Qt, a key's name alone and a menu line's key after its tab. On the reviewed patch it found 30 sentences: the reviewer's 13 and 17 more (Undo/Redo status lines, the capture proposal, the Files room tips, the screensaver, the intake tip, the tool atlas placeholder, the Field brief, the word-keeping note, the Gemini setup). All 30 now name what to click instead, or nothing. 15 sentences that keep a key are listed in KEYS_CODE_KEPT, each with a reason. Most are a key the owner presses with nothing to click instead, and I report them as findings. A new test fails while any unreviewed sentence remains. (3) should_fix: the desk-light limit is now stated as CIE L* under 65. In effect it was L* 62, so it is loosened by about 3 L*, and this is said in the test. KEYS false positives are fixed. named_in keeps the key text in its own variable. The Full Screen tip no longer says 'line'. GETTING_STARTED step 4 names her kp logo. boss_theme's LEGACY note now records that the Return thread's writing box turned from yellow to blue in Kasandra. colour_vision now has a 'cue' meaning, lets 'chosen' include the menu bar and 'ready' include the pointer's halo, and explains the threshold instead of calling it 'usual'. That adds 11 reviewed pairs and rewrites 2: Graphite has 32 pairs under 10, Kasandra 15, and none is unreviewed. Two items are left for the owner to judge by eye: the stepped writing-line light and the Field rings under overlapping sheets. In the copy, 23 affected modules pass in both looks (489 tests per look, 0 failures).

decisions: must_fix 2: the tools/check_head_ui.py hunk is dropped, as the review asked. The checks item deletes that file, and the changed line could not be reached anyway.

Guard for keys the walk cannot reach: I added a sibling sweep (keys_in_code) and did not widen the walk. It reads string constants in workbench/ the way in_code reads her earlier name. Machine text is set aside: docstrings and comments, arguments to QKeySequence/QShortcut/setShortcut(s)/re.compile, shortcut= keywords, a string that is only a key's name (KEY_SPEC: 'Ctrl+Shift+N', 'F7 or Ctrl+Shift+B', 'PgUp  PgDn') and the text after a menu line's tab (tool_faces cuts it). A known hole: a tip set to a bare key name would pass. The code shows none. document_qt's format buttons have accessible descriptions built as 'Ctrl B' + ' · applies…', so they slip through. They are read to a screen reader and never printed, so I left them and report them.

Kept with a reason in KEYS_CODE_KEPT, as findings for the owner rather than deletions. The Field's painted key labels ('Esc  close', '1  take the step', 'G  keep it as a page', 'Esc  back'): each is also a click target that does what its key does (field_qt._key_of and press_key), the Field's design since 0.5, so changing it is the owner's call. The console's 'Press Enter again to run it as written; … press Esc to leave it': an operation that asks is approved by sending the same line again, and the console has no button for that. The Explore descriptor 'a group of rows; Right or Enter opens it': it is shown only after F1, to someone already on the keyboard. The ARC-OS console games and the Godot starter's text (games played with keys). workbench/app.py, the old Tk workbench, which no module imports. version.py's lineage.

The Help menu's 'Keyboard Shortcuts' page (qt_app.show_keys) lists keys by design, and only someone who asks for it opens it. Its rows are bare key names, so the sweep passes them. I report it to the owner and did not change it.

Wording chosen for the fixes. Name what to click: 'Undo takes it back' / 'Redo brings it back', as context_menu already said; 'Stop ends it'; 'Next Problem goes to the first error'; 'Larger prose and Smaller prose, in View, adjust prose'; 'Open in Universal Viewer…, in File, shows any file'; 'Double-click a row to open it' (the list's itemDoubleClicked opens it); 'click it to open it' for a room sheet in the Field; 'The arrow at the line's end keeps this word' (submit_line runs a word line, and its tip says 'Do this to your words'); 'then Capture… in the head row'. Or drop the key: '(Space)', '(Esc)', '(F9)', the empty workspace foot keeps only the title, '; press Enter' in the atlas placeholder, 'press a key' on the screensaver (the pointer still returns, and so does any key). The engineering game buttons 'Left (A)' and 'Right (D)' lost their letters too, to match 'Flap'.

Desk-light limit: I kept the corrected measure and set the limit as perceptual lightness, CIE L* under 65. That is the same scale the colour-vision tool uses through Lab. It is a change from 0.5.0's L* 62 in effect, made so that Kasandra's 0.8.3 tone (L* 63.5) passes, and the test comment says so. look.patch's luminance 0.4 (L* 69.5) was looser than it needed to be.

colour_vision gaps. A meaning can now wear several colours, and a pair is as close as its two closest colours: 'chosen' adds BAR, and 'ready' adds the pointer's halo (HALO = VIOLET_PALE in her look, as pointer.drawn draws it). 'cue' is a new meaning (CUE_EDGE: a status word, a heading's rule, a primary button, a band's rule, a prompt), and its sign is that it marks no state on a row or sheet. No palette colour was changed. The threshold of 10 is now described as this check's own choice, several times the just noticeable difference (Mahy et al. 1994, 2.3 in CIE76), not as a published constant. HALO repeats pointer.drawn's rule instead of reading it. If pointer.py changes its halo, this table will not notice.

LEGACY #f8edc9 -> CUE: the decision stands, because a place to write is not a highlight. The boss_theme note now places the visible change: in Kasandra the Return thread's writing box (return_thread_qt ReturnWriting) turns from her yellow #5a3f0c to her blue CUE #1d3d63.

release_note: Tips, notes and status lines no longer name keyboard keys. Where a key was the only hint, they now name the button or menu row to use, such as Undo, Stop, Next Problem or Larger prose. A test now reads every sentence in the program's code and fails if a key name comes back. The few that remain (the Field's clickable key labels, the console's typed approval and the games) are on a reviewed list. The colour-vision check now also covers the menu bar, the pointer's halo and the cue colours, and every pair those eyes cannot tell apart has its word or shape on record.
